author: EthanJPerez
text: This is an impressive effort towards using human feedback to help train language models

quoted.text: We've fine-tuned GPT-2 using human feedback for tasks such as summarizing articles, matching the preferences of human labelers (if not always our own). We're hoping this brings safety methods closer to machines learning values by talking with humans. https://t.co/ok9jeMP5zj

author: EthanJPerez
text: @liu_haokun @siddkaramcheti @jaseweston @douwekiela @kchonyc Yes, you could use other interpretability methods to find evidence (we just picked one method). Using better interpretability methods may result in better evidence

author: EthanJPerez
text: @siddkaramcheti @jaseweston @douwekiela @kchonyc So we test if our automatically-discovered evidence is useful. We find that using evidence 1) helps people answer questions faster and 2) improves how well Q&A models generalize to harder questions

author: EthanJPerez
text: @siddkaramcheti @jaseweston @douwekiela @kchonyc Doing so gives us evidence that is general (good evidence to people and not that model-specific)

author: EthanJPerez
text: @siddkaramcheti @jaseweston @douwekiela @kchonyc We get Q&A models to help us by probing them to find what they consider to be strong evidence

author: EthanJPerez
text: @siddkaramcheti @jaseweston @douwekiela @kchonyc It’s hard work to find evidence for a stance/answer to a question

author: EthanJPerez
text:
What evidence do people find convincing? Often, the same evidence that Q&A models find convincing.
